item.title: AKS
item.description:
Quick Start with AKS

Manage your AKS clusters with Meshery. Deploy Meshery inside your AKS cluster (in-cluster), or run it outside of AKS (out-of-cluster) and connect it to your cluster. Note: We recommend installing Meshery in your AKS clusters.

Prerequisites

  1. Install the Meshery command line client, mesheryctl.
  2. Install kubectl on your local machine.
  3. Install Azure CLI, configured for your environment.
  4. Access to an active AKS cluster in one of your resource groups.

Also see: Install Meshery on Kubernetes

item.title: DigitalOcean
item.description:
Quick Start with DigitalOcean

Deploy and manage your DigitalOcean infrastructure with Meshery. You can run Meshery on DigitalOcean in two ways: out-of-cluster using Docker on a Droplet, or in-cluster on a DigitalOcean Kubernetes (DOKS) cluster. Note: We recommend installing Meshery in your DOKS cluster.

Prerequisites

  1. Install the Meshery command line client, mesheryctl.
  2. Install kubectl on your local machine.
  3. Install the DigitalOcean CLI (doctl), authenticated for your account.
  4. A DigitalOcean account with access to either a Droplet or an active DOKS cluster.

Also see: Install Meshery on Kubernetes

item.title: Helm
item.description:
Install Meshery on Kubernetes Using Helm

Prerequisites

  1. Install Helm and kubectl on your local machine.
  2. Access to the cluster where you want to deploy Meshery.
  3. A kubeconfig whose current context points at that cluster.

Install Meshery on Your Kubernetes Cluster Using Helm 

	

		helm repo add meshery https://meshery.io/charts/
helm install meshery meshery/meshery --namespace meshery --create-namespace

Optionally, customize the callback URL that your Remote Provider redirects to after sign-in:

	

		helm install meshery meshery/meshery --namespace meshery --set env.MESHERY_SERVER_CALLBACK_URL=https://custom-host --create-namespace

Customizing Meshery’s Installation with values.yaml

Meshery’s Helm chart supports many configuration options. See the Meshery Helm chart and Meshery Operator Helm Chart for more information.

item.title: KubeSphere
item.description:
Quick Start with KubeSphere

Prerequisites

1. Install the Meshery command line client, mesheryctl .

Meshery is the open source, cloud native manager for Kubernetes, all kinds of cloud native infrastructure, and their workloads.

This guide walks you through deploying Meshery from the KubeSphere App Store.

Prerequisites

  • Enable the OpenPitrix system (the KubeSphere App Store).
  • Create a workspace, a project, and a user account. The account must be a platform regular user, invited to the project as an operator with the operator role. This guide uses the user project-regular, the project demo-project, and the workspace demo-workspace. For details, see Create Workspaces, Projects, Users and Roles in the KubeSphere documentation.

item.title: Minikube
item.description:
Quick Start with Minikube

Meshery can manage your Minikube clusters, and it is especially useful for multi-cluster management and deployments.

To manage your Minikube cluster, Meshery Server must discover it and add it as a Kubernetes connection.

Once your cluster is a connection, you can use Meshery to deploy your Meshery Designs to it. To learn more, see Deploying Meshery Designs.

There are two ways to create this connection:

  1. Deploy Meshery in Minikube (in-cluster).
  2. Deploy Meshery with Docker and connect it to Minikube (out-of-cluster).

Note: We recommend installing Meshery in your Minikube clusters.
